scenarioStory.history: 62-year-old male was playing in a recreational softball game when teammates report he suddenly grabbed his chest, said he felt "lightheaded," and collapsed to the ground while standing near first base. A teammate who is an off-duty ICU nurse recognized the collapse as cardiac arrest, called 911, and began chest compressions immediately — no more than 15-20 seconds after the patient went down. No AED was available on site. Bystander CPR has been ongoing since collapse.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 62-year-old male supine on the infield, unresponsive, with a bystander performing chest compressions. Rapid assessment confirms no pulse, no respirations, and agonal/absent breathing. → CPR & Pads Applied: Crew has taken over high-quality chest compressions from the bystander and applied defibrillator pads. Monitor confirms coarse ventricular fibrillation. → First Shock Delivered: Crew delivers the first defibrillation and immediately resumes chest compressions for a full 2-minute cycle without pausing for a pulse check. → ROSC Achieved: After one 2-minute cycle of CPR following the single shock, the pulse/rhythm check reveals an organized sinus tachycardia with a palpable carotid pulse. Compressions are stopped and post-ROSC care begins. → Post-ROSC Care & Transport: Patient remains unresponsive but hemodynamically improving. Crew titrates oxygenation and ventilation, acquires a 12-lead EKG to screen for STEMI, checks glucose, and prepares for transport to an appropriate receiving facility.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 62-year-old male supine on the infield, unresponsive, with a bystander performing chest compressions. Rapid assessment confirms no pulse, no respirations, and agonal/absent breathing.
relatedChecklist: Confirm pulselessness and apnea rapidly; do not delay treatment for full assessment

scenarioEvents.name: CPR & Pads Applied
scenarioEvents.description: Crew has taken over high-quality chest compressions from the bystander and applied defibrillator pads. Monitor confirms coarse ventricular fibrillation.
relatedChecklist: Take over compressions from bystander; apply pads and analyze rhythm without delay
Maintain compression rate 100-120/min, depth 2-2.4 inches, allow full chest recoil
Apply passive oxygenation via NRB with OPA for first compression cycles; do not interrupt compressions

scenarioEvents.name: First Shock Delivered
scenarioEvents.description: Crew delivers the first defibrillation and immediately resumes chest compressions for a full 2-minute cycle without pausing for a pulse check.
relatedChecklist: Defibrillate at 120 J (first shock, Zoll biphasic per protocol)
Resume compressions immediately post-shock; no pulse check for 2 minutes
Obtain IV/IO access without interrupting chest compressions
Pre-charge defibrillator during compressions to minimize peri-shock pause

scenarioEvents.name: ROSC Achieved
scenarioEvents.description: After one 2-minute cycle of CPR following the single shock, the pulse/rhythm check reveals an organized sinus tachycardia with a palpable carotid pulse. Compressions are stopped and post-ROSC care begins.
relatedChecklist: Recognize ROSC; stop compressions once organized rhythm with pulse confirmed
Support airway/breathing and circulation; identify likely cause of arrest
Monitor closely for re-arrest via cardiac monitor, EtCO2, and perfusion signs

scenarioEvents.name: Post-ROSC Care & Transport
scenarioEvents.description: Patient remains unresponsive but hemodynamically improving. Crew titrates oxygenation and ventilation, acquires a 12-lead EKG to screen for STEMI, checks glucose, and prepares for transport to an appropriate receiving facility.
relatedChecklist: Titrate oxygen to SpO2 94-98%; avoid hyperoxygenation
Ventilate 8-10 breaths/min; target EtCO2 35-45 mmHg, avoid hyperventilation
Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes to screen for STEMI; transmit and notify receiving hospital if positive
Transport to a cath-capable facility if STEMI or reversible cardiac cause identified
Check blood glucose; treat per Hypoglycemia Guideline if low, notify hospital if high
Avoid hyperthermia; do not apply warm blankets or excessive heat exposure

scenarioEvents.name: Compressions Delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew pauses to perform a full assessment before taking over compressions, allowing a prolonged hands-off interval. Perfusion continues to deteriorate as fibrillation coarseness begins to diminish.
relatedChecklist: Recognize delay; immediately resume compressions and apply pads without further assessment

scenarioEvents.name: Refractory VF
scenarioEvents.description: The 2-minute rhythm/pulse check following the first shock shows persistent coarse VF with no pulse, requiring escalation to a second shock, epinephrine, and consideration of antiarrhythmic therapy.
relatedChecklist: Deliver second defibrillation at 150 J (Zoll biphasic escalation)
Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO (fixed adult dose, 0.1 mg/kg capped at max 1 mg); repeat q3-5min
Consider Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO for shock-refractory VF/pulseless VT
